name: Prego rolls
summary: Thin garlicky steak seared hot and fast, then tucked into a soft Portuguese roll with the peri-peri pan juices: the Portuguese-South African café steak roll.
about: Prego means "nail" in Portuguese. The steak roll came to South Africa with Portuguese and Mozambican-Portuguese families and settled into cafés and takeaways, where it gained a spicy peri-peri sauce. Families make it at home on a Saturday, with chips on the side.

ingredients.name: Peri-peri sauce
ingredients.note: mild or hot, plus extra to serve

steps: Lay the steaks between two sheets of baking paper and flatten them with a rolling pin to about 5 mm thick. Trim off any fat.

Mix the garlic, 2 tbsp of the oil, the peri-peri sauce, paprika, bay leaves and lemon juice in a dish. Turn the steaks in it to coat and leave for at least 10 minutes (or up to overnight in the fridge). Season with salt and pepper just before cooking.

Heat a large heavy frying pan over high heat until very hot. Add the rest of the oil and half the butter, then sear the steaks two at a time for 1–1½ minutes a side, until browned outside and still slightly pink inside. Move them to a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium, scrape the leftover marinade (without the bay leaves) into the pan with the wine and the remaining butter, and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until slightly reduced and glossy.
Toast the cut sides of the rolls in a dry pan or under the oven grill for 1–2 minutes, until golden.
Return the steaks to the pan for 30 seconds to coat them in the sauce. Fill each roll with a steak, spoon over the pan juices and add extra peri-peri sauce to taste. Serve straight away with chips.
prepNote: Flatten and marinate the steaks the night before; cook just before serving.
